title: The multi-selection specimen draws its own group frame
goal: On the page that teaches how selection looks, the picture showing two objects selected at once draws its group outline with its own one-off code instead of the standard one, so the page breaks the rule it is teaching. This makes that picture use the shared frame like everything else.
notes: pages/lang-selection.html around line 396: the multi-select specimen uses a page-local .lx-group div plus four .handle spans with inline left/top/right/bottom offsets, and no .sel-ring. selection.css already ships .selwrap.multi (dashed .sel-ring, handles suppressed) for exactly this case, so the specimen should be .selwrap.multi with data-sel-frame and the .lx-group rule deleted. Note the caption says the group frame KEEPS its handles while .selwrap.multi drops them (you transform the group, not a member) - reconcile the copy with the component rather than re-adding handles. Found by the browser sweep in canvas-selection-frames-come-from-one-shared-hel: it is the only orphan handle set left in the study.
acceptance: The two-objects-selected picture on the selection language page uses the standard multi-selection frame
The corner grabs sit where the shared frame puts them, with no hand-set offsets
The page still reads the same: a thin outline per object, one frame around both, and a count

log.note: Staging check: this serves design-system (staged next, not now). Kept it because it is a ten-minute conformance fix on the page that TEACHES the selection rule, and the sibling mock-conformance tasks ahead of it in the queue were all completed rather than dropped. Not expanded beyond the one specimen.

Adversarial review of the ask, BEFORE building. The notes told me to reconcile the caption to the component: .selwrap.multi hides the union frame's handles, so the caption saying 'the group frame keeps its handles' should change. I disagree and did the opposite. A frame with no grabs says 'this cannot be resized', and resizing two selected objects together is the most ordinary thing in a design tool; every mainstream tool gives a multi-selection a resize box. The page's own Do list already says 'give the group frame the only handles in a multi-select', and selection.css's own comment says 'you transform the group, not one member of it' and then hides the group's handles, which contradicts its own sentence. Dashing the union ring is worse still: dashed already means marquee (the band you are dragging right now) in this family, so spending it on a committed selection makes both unreadable. .selwrap.multi also had zero usages in 55 pages, so nothing depended on it.

Built: the union frame is now a plain <div class="selwrap" data-sel-frame="2 selected"> hung on the union box, so selection.js builds the ring, the four grabs and the tag. Deleted .lx-group, .lx-thin and .lx-count from the page. Replaced .selwrap.multi in shared/components/selection.css with .mem-ring (accent, 1px at 70%, hugs bounds) documented as the sixth member of the bounds-ring family, plus a comment recording why the old rule was wrong.

Adversarial review of the built thing, in the browser. Two problems the mock had and I inherited: (1) the union frame's corner grabs hung 4.7px outside the canvas and were clipped by the plinth's overflow, because the specimen was 160px wide in a ~166px canvas and the old 9px orbit hid it. Narrowed the specimen to 130px, the same width the Single card next to it uses, so the pair now reads as a set and nothing clips (worst clearance on the card is now 24px). (2) The old member outlines orbited their objects by 3px, which is exactly the 'do not orbit the bounds' drift the frame rule exists to kill; .mem-ring hugs at inset -1px. Honest residual: at the union's extremes a member outline sits directly under the union ring and is hidden there, so each object shows its thin outline on only two of its four sides. That is geometrically unavoidable (the union is by definition touched by its members) and is what real tools look like, so I left it.

Verified: check-selection 55 pages pass and the declared-frame count went 7 -> 8; check-states and check-elevation pass; no console errors; specimen checked in dark and light. Same-page cleanup while I was in there: section 06's snapping specimen had hand-set -11px handle offsets and a -28px mtag override, both now removed. No audit written: this is design-study conformance, not a playtestable app feature.

lang-selection's Variants > Multi-select specimen is now a plain .selwrap with data-sel-frame, so the shared component builds its ring, grabs and count tag; .lx-group/.lx-thin/.lx-count deleted. .selwrap.multi (dead, and it hid the union frame's handles, contradicting the page's own Do rule) replaced in selection.css by .mem-ring, the member outline. Also unclipped the specimen's grabs and removed section 06's hand-set offsets. Verified in the browser in both themes; check-selection/states/elevation pass. Commit 4ca611b.
